argument_summary: The admissible record does not support treating rollout controls as curing the Spanish-language billing limitation. It does support a narrower certification position: aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the launch is limited to a reversible 5% rollout with monitoring and rollback. Under the stated policy, that is supportable only if certification is understood as a disclosed-risk launch posture, not as proof the limitation was resolved. The audit concern is therefore overstated to the extent it treats the packet as claiming controls eliminate the disclosure issue; the stronger reading is that certification can proceed only with an explicit caveat that the exposed limitation remains material and must stay disclosed in the launch record.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy cuts both ways. It rejects the theory that rollout controls alone remove disclosure duties while the affected segment remains exposed. But it does not forbid certification categorically; it permits launch so long as the material limitation is treated as disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. On this record, approved risk acceptance is absent and exposure remains, so the supportable policy position is caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure, not unconditional compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: No urgency claim is needed. The governance-efficient outcome is to avoid escalation beyond the narrow compliance issue if the auditor can record certification only as caveated compliance requiring express disclosure of the live limitation.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence here proving the exact certification or model-card text already contains the required explicit disclosure.
The risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not cover the Spanish-language billing exposure.
The affected Spanish-language billing use case remains exposed in the initial cohort, so rollout controls do not by themselves satisfy the policy predicate.
